Medicine-08.question: ২) Both sexes affected but only inherited through female meiosis in
৬) Burrow is a lesion found in
৭) Antibody that makes defense against parasitic infection
৯) Transmission of 50% offspring irrespective of gender
১৩) Most common variant of Downs syndrome
Medicine-08.exp:
The most common variant of Down syndrome is caused by meiotic nondisjunction, resulting in free trisomy 21 (47,+21). It accounts for about 95% of all cases.

Although the karyotype is trisomy 21, the variant/mechanism is nondisjunction.

Why the other options are incorrect

  • A. Trisomy — Describes the chromosomal state, not the specific variant/mechanism.

  • B. Mosaic — Accounts for only 1–2% of cases.

  • C. Nondisjunction — Correct. Causes about 95% of Down syndrome cases.

  • D. Translocation — Accounts for 3–4% of cases, usually Robertsonian translocation.

High-yield Recall

Variant of Down Syndrome Frequency
Nondisjunction (Free trisomy 21) ~95%
Robertsonian translocation ~3–4%
Mosaicism ~1–2%

Exam pearl: The commonest mechanism (variant) of Down syndrome is meiotic nondisjunction, producing free trisomy 21.

Medicine-08.question: ১৪) Antibody that is particularly important at mucosal surface
১৬) Initiation code in genetics
Medicine-08.exp:
The initiation (start) codon in mRNA is AUG, which:

  • Signals the start of protein synthesis (translation).

  • Codes for methionine in eukaryotes (and N-formylmethionine (fMet) in prokaryotes).

Why the other options are incorrect

  • A. AUG — Correct. Universal start codon.

  • B. UAG — Stop codon (amber).

  • C. UAA — Stop codon (ochre).

  • D. GAU — Codes for aspartic acid.

High-yield Recall

Codon Function
AUG Start codon (Methionine)
UAA Stop codon (Ochre)
UAG Stop codon (Amber)
UGA Stop codon (Opal)

Exam pearl: AUG is the universal initiation codon, while UAA, UAG, and UGA are the three termination (stop) codons.

Medicine-08.question: ১৭) STI that can transmit through transplacental route
১৮) Gram negative diplococci in microscopy is indicative of
১৯) Affected males related through unaffected females
২০) Treatment of choice for syphilis during pregnancy
২১) Chronic granulomatous lesion in benign tertiary syphilis is called
২৪) Silvery scale is a feature of
Medicine-08.exp:
Psoriasis is characterized by well-demarcated erythematous plaques covered with silvery-white scales. The lesions commonly occur on:

  • Extensor surfaces (elbows and knees)

  • Scalp

  • Lumbosacral region

Other classic signs include:

  • Auspitz sign (pinpoint bleeding after scale removal)

  • Koebner phenomenon (lesions develop at sites of trauma)

Why the other options are incorrect

  • A. Scabies — Characterized by burrows and intense nocturnal itching.

  • B. Psoriasis — Correct. Classical silvery scales over erythematous plaques.

  • C. Eczema — Presents with erythema, vesicles, oozing, and lichenification rather than silvery scales.

  • D. Tinea — Typically shows annular lesions with peripheral scaling and central clearing.

High-yield Recall

Skin Disease Characteristic Feature
Psoriasis Silvery-white scales
Scabies Burrows, nocturnal pruritus
Eczema Vesicles, oozing, lichenification
Tinea corporis Ring-shaped lesion with central clearing

Exam pearl: Silvery-white scales on well-defined plaques over the extensor surfaces are the hallmark of psoriasis.

Medicine-08.question: ২৬) Antibody that can be transported through placenta
২৭) Not a cell of innate immune system
৩৪) Acute cellular transplant rejection occurs due to which type of hypersensitivity?
৩৬) Commonest form of psoriasis in children
৩৭) Comedone is a lesion found in
Medicine-08.exp:
A comedone is the primary lesion of acne vulgaris, resulting from obstruction of the pilosebaceous follicle by keratin and sebum.

Types:

  • Open comedone → Blackhead

  • Closed comedone → Whitehead

Why the other options are incorrect

  • A. Scabies — Characterized by burrows and intense nocturnal itching.

  • B. Eczema — Presents with erythema, vesicles, oozing, and lichenification.

  • C. Psoriasis — Characterized by well-defined plaques with silvery scales.

  • D. Acne — Correct. Comedones are the hallmark lesion.

High-yield Recall

Disease Characteristic Lesion
Acne vulgaris Comedones (blackheads & whiteheads)
Scabies Burrows
Psoriasis Silvery scales
Eczema Vesicles, oozing, lichenification

Exam pearl: Comedones are pathognomonic of acne vulgaris and are absent in rosacea.

Medicine-08.question: ৩৮) Gene related to Prader–Willi syndrome
Medicine-08.exp:
Prader–Willi syndrome (PWS) is caused by loss of expression of paternally inherited genes in chromosome 15q11–q13. The SNRPN gene lies within this critical region and is commonly associated with Prader–Willi syndrome.

Mechanisms include:

  • Paternal deletion (most common)

  • Maternal uniparental disomy

  • Imprinting defect

Clinical features:

  • Neonatal hypotonia

  • Hyperphagia leading to obesity

  • Intellectual disability

  • Hypogonadism

  • Short stature

Why the other options are incorrect

  • A. UBE3A — Associated with Angelman syndrome (loss of maternal UBE3A).

  • B. SNRPN — Correct. Associated with Prader–Willi syndrome.

  • C. CDKN1C — Associated with Beckwith–Wiedemann syndrome.

  • D. IGF2 — Also involved in Beckwith–Wiedemann syndrome through imprinting abnormalities.

High-yield Recall

Syndrome Gene/Defect
Prader–Willi syndrome SNRPN, paternal 15q11–q13 deletion/imprinting defect
Angelman syndrome UBE3A, maternal 15q11–q13 deletion
Beckwith–Wiedemann syndrome CDKN1C, IGF2 imprinting abnormalities

Exam pearl: Chromosome 15 imprinting disorders: "Paternal deletion → Prader–Willi (SNRPN); Maternal deletion → Angelman (UBE3A)."

Medicine-08.question: ৩৯) Conversion of 7-dehydrocholesterol to vitamin D is done by
Medicine-08.exp:
Keratinocytes of the stratum basale and stratum spinosum contain 7-dehydrocholesterol, which is converted to previtamin D₃ by ultraviolet B (UVB) sunlight. Previtamin D₃ is then converted to vitamin D₃ (cholecalciferol).

Why the other options are incorrect

  • A. Keratinocyte — Correct. Site of cutaneous vitamin D₃ synthesis.

  • B. Dendritic (Langerhans) cell — Antigen-presenting cell; not involved in vitamin D synthesis.

  • C. Merkel cell — Mechanoreceptor cell for touch.

  • D. Melanocyte — Produces melanin; does not convert 7-dehydrocholesterol to vitamin D.

High-yield Recall

Skin Cell Main Function
Keratinocyte Vitamin D synthesis, keratin production
Melanocyte Melanin production
Langerhans (dendritic) cell Antigen presentation
Merkel cell Touch sensation

Exam pearl: Vitamin D synthesis begins in keratinocytes when UVB converts 7-dehydrocholesterol to previtamin D₃, which then becomes cholecalciferol (vitamin D₃).

Medicine-08.question: ৪০) Molluscum contagiosum is caused by
Medicine-08.exp:
Molluscum contagiosum is a benign viral skin infection caused by the Molluscum contagiosum virus (MCV), which belongs to the Poxvirus family.

Clinical features:

  • Small, pearly, flesh-colored papules

  • Central umbilication

  • Common in children, sexually active adults, and immunocompromised patients (e.g., HIV)

Why the other options are incorrect

  • A. HHV-8 — Causes Kaposi sarcoma.

  • B. Parvovirus — Causes erythema infectiosum (fifth disease).

  • C. Pox virus — Correct. Causes molluscum contagiosum.

  • D. Papilloma virus (HPV) — Causes warts (verrucae) and genital warts.

High-yield Recall

Virus Disease
Poxvirus Molluscum contagiosum
HPV Warts, condyloma acuminata
HHV-8 Kaposi sarcoma
Parvovirus B19 Erythema infectiosum, aplastic crisis

Exam pearl: The hallmark of molluscum contagiosum is multiple pearly, umbilicated papules caused by a Poxvirus.

Medicine-08.question: ৪১) Which cells in the skin are primarily involved in antigen presentation?
Medicine-08.exp:
Langerhans' cells are specialized dendritic cells located mainly in the epidermis. They are the principal antigen-presenting cells (APCs) of the skin. They capture antigens, migrate to regional lymph nodes, and present them to T lymphocytes, initiating the adaptive immune response.

Why the other options are incorrect

  • A. Keratinocytes — Form the skin barrier and produce keratin; they are not the primary APCs.

  • B. Langerhans' cells — Correct. The main antigen-presenting cells of the epidermis.

  • C. Merkel cells — Mechanoreceptor cells responsible for touch sensation.

  • D. T lymphocytes — Respond to antigens but do not function as professional antigen-presenting cells.

High-yield Recall

Skin Cell Main Function
Langerhans' cell Antigen presentation (APC)
Keratinocyte Keratin production, skin barrier, vitamin D synthesis
Melanocyte Melanin production
Merkel cell Touch sensation

Exam pearl: Langerhans' cells are dendritic antigen-presenting cells found in the epidermis and are essential for initiating cell-mediated immunity.

Medicine-08.question: ৪৩) In Down’s syndrome there is high incidence of
৪৬) All of the following are indicative of PID except
৪৮) Antibody that is highly effective at agglutinating pathogen
৫০) Cardinal symptom of immunodeficiency
Medicine-08.exp:
The cardinal clinical feature of immunodeficiency is recurrent, severe, persistent, or unusual infections caused by common or opportunistic pathogens.

Depending on the immune defect, patients may also develop autoimmunity, allergies, or malignancies, but infection is the hallmark presentation.

Why the other options are incorrect

  • A. Autoimmunity — May occur in some immunodeficiency disorders but is not the cardinal feature.

  • B. Infection — Correct. Recurrent infections are the hallmark of immunodeficiency.

  • C. Hypersensitivity — Characteristic of allergic disorders, not immunodeficiency.

  • D. Rejection — Refers to transplant immunology, not immunodeficiency.

High-yield Recall

Immune Disorder Cardinal Feature
Immunodeficiency Recurrent infections
Autoimmune disease Loss of self-tolerance
Hypersensitivity Exaggerated immune response
Transplant rejection Immune response against graft

Exam pearl: Think immunodeficiency whenever a patient has recurrent, severe, opportunistic, or unusual infections, especially from early childhood.
